overview: The committee reviewed the preliminary fiscal year 2027 budget proposal, which features a significant funding gap, and received several student and program presentations. Key actions included approving the consent agenda and authorizing the payment of overdue invoices from the previous fiscal year.

items.title: Executive Session
items.summary: The committee voted to enter executive session to conduct strategy for contract negotiations with various non-union personnel and school administrators.

items.title: Consent Agenda
items.summary: The committee approved various routine items including payroll, budget transfers, science prize donations, and a field trip to New Hampshire. Approved.

items.title: Mustang Moments
items.summary: Students and staff presented on the Missituk School Council activities, the Unified PE Program's inclusive athletic initiatives, and a state-wide youth poster contest winner.

items.title: Introduction of Transportation Director
items.summary: The superintendent formally introduced Ina Williams as the new district-wide transportation manager.

items.title: FY27 Preliminary Budget Recommendations
items.summary: Finance staff presented a $94 million preliminary budget request, noting that unavoidable cost increases and student needs have created a $5 million gap relative to projected city funding. Discussion focused on the potential necessity of staffing reductions if additional revenue is not secured.

items.title: Gone Green Overdue Invoices
items.summary: The committee authorized the payment of $48,665.51 for fiscal year 2025 electrical services that were not processed due to previous staffing transitions. Approved.

items.title: Student Survey on Lunch and Transportation
items.summary: Student representatives presented survey data highlighting cafeteria overcrowding and student dissatisfaction with bus railings and the lack of late-bus options.

items.title: MSBA Project Update
items.summary: The chair of the building committee provided an update on the high school construction project, including the selection of six design options for further study and ongoing grant applications.

items.title: Condolences
items.summary: The committee held a moment of silence for David P. Skerry and Lot Max Parisian.
